items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I knew what to do I think because I had grown up with a lot of blues and boogie woogie piano records by Meade Lux Lewis and Albert Ammons and Pete Johnson and all those people.

ctx.x: But what kind of adjustment was there for players who were let’s say swing oriented, to start playing that different style? Was it a big deal?

Well yes and no. As Milt Hinton used to say “yes and then again, no.” Of course there were adjustments to be made. Rock ‘n roll was a blues style basically and I knew what to do I think because I had grown up with a lot of blues and boogie woogie piano records by Meade Lux Lewis and Albert Ammons and Pete Johnson and all those people. And so it wasn’t all that remarkable to figure out how to play along with some of those people. And many of them really were blues singers. Then there was another kind of rock ‘n…
No you didn’t talk about Frankie.
